answer: Influence comes only from escrowed tasks verified by randomly assigned peers; rewards wait through a challenge period. New identities begin with no reputation, so splitting one operator into many accounts adds no voting power. Each account must lock scarce collateral, which is slashed if claims fail. A river of tasks can feed a lagoon of reviews, while karst-like patterns in shared funding reveal linked accounts. Sybils cost capital and risk forfeiture.
